To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the transcription of rRNA is a tightly controlled process; (2) the transcription of a rDNA gene is regulated at multiple levels; (3) rRNA transcription is regulated by a number of different mechanisms including: (i) transcriptional initiation, (ii) transcription elongation, and (iii) transcription termination.
the transcription of the rRNA gene cluster of the human parasite Trypanosoma brucei is regulated by a novel, highly efficient mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of ribosomal RNA gene transcription.
the transcription of rDNA in eukaryotic cells, the structure and function of the rRNA genes and the regulation of rRNA synthesis in response to growth, development, and environmental stress.
the molecular mechanisms that control the transcription of eukaryotic rRNA genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rDNA transcription is highly regulated and efficient.
the transcription of rRNA genes is regulated by the availability of the RNA polymerase I transcription factor, UBF.
transcription of rDNA occurs at the level of rRNA genes in the nucleolus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of transcription of the rDNA is achieved by the interaction of several proteins with the rDNA, which in turn leads to a modulation of the transcriptional activity of the rDNA.
the transcriptional machinery of eukaryotes has been conserved throughout evolution, but the regulation of transcription of rDNA has become increasingly complex.
we are trying to understand how the transcription machinery of eukaryotic cells recognizes and initiates the synthesis of ribosomal RNA genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 5' end of the 18S rRNA is transcribed from the promoter region, which is the region of the DNA that contains the binding site for RNA polymerase, and the 18S, the 28S, and the 5.8 rRNA genes all start at the same location.
the transcription of the 45S rRNA precursor is a highly regulated process that is coordinated with the cell cycle.
the transcription of rRNA genes is regulated in a way that is similar to the transcription of protein-encoding genes.
